Internal helper: jsave's undeclared-stray release note

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_jsave_release_notes.Rd

The RELEASE-side note of the S239 mint/observe/release framework: jsave() is the boundary past which the package can no longer reach the data, so an undeclared suspicious code written to a declaration-carrying format is reported ONCE, when the frame's own metadata supplies the evidence. Fires only when all three hold: the target format carries declarations (gated at the call site); another column declares missing values in the same style (SPSS-form numeric declarations – tag-form columns are self-declaring, so no undeclared-tag state exists and tags do not testify about numeric strays); and an undeclared suspicious code sits on a column. Silent when the frame declares nothing anywhere (the pure-guess case). Groups by column when codes differ; the remedy is a runnable declare-then-resave pair.

Usage

.jst_jsave_release_notes(
  data,
  data_name,
  file_arg,
  code_name = data_name,
  assign_line = NULL,
  clean_names = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

The data frame as written (post any preserve.declarations collapse, so a stripped frame has no evidence and stays silent), carrying the data frame's own variable names.

data_name

Character. The frame's display name.

file_arg

Character. The normalized (forward-slash) target path, echoed into the resave line. Never the raw file argument: a Windows backslash path inside the quoted recipe is a parse error on paste.

code_name

Character. The data frame as the lines name it: data_name, or mydata for data given as an expression.

assign_line

Character(1) or NULL: the line that makes mydata, " mydata <- <the expression>", first in the block.

clean_names

Logical: the call's clean.names, kept in the save line.

Value

Character scalar note, or NULL when nothing fires.

Details

Since Session 388 (Fix Slate 27; printed calls run, S343) the lines run as printed after every save that gives the note. After clean.names = TRUE the note names the data frame's own variable, which jsave() passes in place of the file's name – the declare line named the file's name, which the data frame does not hold – and the save line keeps clean.names = TRUE, without which it stopped on the names. A name that R reads only in backticks gets them. Given an expression as the data, the lines name mydata after the line that makes it, the S339 form, where both had named the expression: modify = TRUE stopped on it, and the save wrote the unchanged data again.
